paper_title: Can LLMs Solve longer Math Word Problems Better
caption: (left) and (right) of scaling up SFT dataset across various model scales in the LLaMA-2 family. The results suggest scaling up model scales and SFT dataset can further improve .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of various LLaMA-2 models on ColeG-E, a mathematical task, under different conditions of Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on various datasets. The horizontal axis represents the model categories, labeled as LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-2-70B, indicating different model sizes. The vertical axis is labeled "ColeG-E (%)", representing the percentage score achieved by the models, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 50 in increments of 10. Each model category is represented by a group of four bars, differentiated by color and pattern: blue with white diagonal lines for "no SFT", orange with white horizontal lines for "+ SFT on D0", purple with white diagonal lines for "+ SFT on D0, D1", and red with white diagonal lines for "+ SFT on D0, D1, D2". For LLaMA-2-7B, the bars have approximate values of 4.5, 20, 28, and 30, respectively. For LLaMA-2-13B, the values are around 8, 32, 37, and 39. For LLaMA-2-70B, the values are approximately 27, 45, 49, and 50. The bars within each group are not sorted, but the models are ordered from smallest to largest on the horizontal axis. The chart effectively visualizes the impact of SFT on different datasets across various model sizes.
